subsystems.name: Mutation engine
subsystems.role: generates functionally equivalent variants of code, memory layout or configuration.

subsystems.name: Genetic optimiser
subsystems.role: evolves a population of variants toward those that best resist known attack techniques.

subsystems.name: Attack sensing and feedback
subsystems.role: detects live intrusion attempts and anomalies, feeding real-world data back to the optimiser.

subsystems.name: Deployment orchestrator
subsystems.role: rolls out new variants quickly and safely across many machines.

subsystems.name: Compatibility and safety layer
subsystems.role: ensures mutations preserve intended function and do not introduce new weaknesses.

buildSteps.title: Map the mutable surface
buildSteps.detail: Identify which parts of the system — code sections, memory addresses, API call orders, configuration values — can be changed without breaking functionality.

buildSteps.title: Implement program transformation
buildSteps.detail: Build tools that automatically rewrite those parts into equivalent but structurally different forms, such as reordering instructions, changing data layouts or inserting harmless noise.

buildSteps.title: Define the fitness function
buildSteps.detail: Specify measurable goals, such as how much a variant raises the cost of a known exploit, how little it slows performance, and how well it preserves behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Build the genetic algorithm
buildSteps.detail: Create a population of candidate variants, mutate and combine them, and select the best performers according to the fitness function over many generations.

buildSteps.title: Instrument live monitoring
buildSteps.detail: Add sensors that detect real attacks and anomalies, then feed that data back so the optimiser learns which mutations actually disrupt adversaries in the field.

buildSteps.title: Create a fast deployment pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Set up systems to push new variants to thousands of endpoints within minutes, with canary testing and automatic rollback if something breaks.

buildSteps.title: Validate with red teams
buildSteps.detail: Run controlled attack exercises against mutated and unmutated versions to confirm that the changes measurably hinder exploitation.

buildSteps.title: Operate continuously
buildSteps.detail: Keep evolving variants as new attack techniques appear, balancing mutation rate against stability and performance overhead.

prerequisites.why: compilers, obfuscators and binary rewriters already change code structure, but doing so safely and at scale is harder.
they provide the search method for exploring huge spaces of possible mutations.
the system needs live signals about what attackers are doing to guide evolution.
frequent legitimate changes must not themselves become an attack vector.
proving that every mutated variant behaves exactly like the original is impractical for large programs today.

pathway.milestone: moving target defence research prototypes and limited commercial tools, such as address space layout randomisation (ASLR), already randomise one layer.
pathway.unlocks: proof that changing the attack surface can break exploits.

pathway.milestone: enterprise pilots for web applications and endpoint software that mutate code or configuration frequently.
pathway.unlocks: real-world data on performance cost and attacker adaptation.

pathway.milestone: integration with CI/CD pipelines so that every build produces a unique, hardened variant.
pathway.unlocks: continuous, automatic defence without manual intervention.

pathway.milestone: autonomous systems that evolve their own defences in response to live attacks, guided by genetic algorithms.
pathway.unlocks: defence that adapts faster than human attackers can reverse-engineer.
